title: Burst capacity runbook: GPU policy notes (Feb 2026)
content:
Sheet: Burst capacity runbook — GPU autoscaling experiments (Feb 2026)

Summary:
This sheet records a set of controlled experiments run against regional GPU pools to validate burst-window scaling behaviour, warm-pool sizing, and step-scaling trigger thresholds. The goal is to identify stable min/warm/max settings and cooldowns that keep p95 inference latency < 220ms for hosted medium workloads while minimizing excess idle GPU hours during short bursts.

Experiment matrix (one row per experimental policy):
Header: policy_id | region | min_gpus | warm_pool | max_gpus | scale_up_step | scale_down_step | cpu_util_target_pct | queue_depth_trigger | cooldown_s | observed_peak_util_pct | p95_latency_ms | tokens_per_sec_per_gpu | avg_idle_hours_per_day | notes
E1 | us-west1 | 8 | 2 | 32 | 4 | 2 | 65 | 120 | 300 | 82 | 198 | 4200 | 1.6 | burst window 5m, step 4 performed well for 10-12min spikes
E2 | us-west1 | 4 | 1 | 24 | 6 | 3 | 75 | 200 | 180 | 91 | 235 | 3600 | 2.9 | aggressive up-step reduced queue but increased cost, higher p95
E3 | us-east1 | 6 | 2 | 28 | 3 | 2 | 60 | 100 | 420 | 78 | 210 | 4400 | 1.1 | long cooldown helped avoid oscillation on diurnal ramp
E4 | eu-west1 | 4 | 1 | 18 | 2 | 1 | 70 | 150 | 240 | 74 | 190 | 4000 | 0.9 | low max sufficient for observed traffic
E5 | ap-southeast1 | 2 | 0 | 12 | 2 | 1 | 65 | 80 | 300 | 86 | 260 | 3300 | 0.6 | higher p95 due to network variance, recommend slightly higher min

Key observations from experiments:
- Warm pool matters for short bursts (<8 minutes): policies with warm_pool >= 2 in US regions reduced p95 by ~25ms compared to warm_pool 0/1 because first-stage cold-starts (container + model init) were amortized.
- Step size tradeoffs: larger scale_up_step (>=4) reduces queue depth quickly but increases overshoot risk and idle hours. Smaller steps (2-3) produced smoother latency at the cost of slightly longer queue drains.
- Cooldown tuning: short cooldowns (<240s) cause oscillation on sawtooth traffic patterns. We observed ping-pong scaling when cooldown < 180s and step sizes > 3. A 300s cooldown was a good middle ground for burst windows of 5-15 minutes.
- Region-specific notes: eu-west1 had more stable traffic and can run tighter max/min; ap-southeast1 showed variable network latency — increase min_gpus by 1 for critical customers in APAC.

Quantitative summary (per-region recommended targets derived from experiments):
Header: region | recommended_min | recommended_warm_pool | recommended_max | recommended_scale_up_step | recommended_cooldown_s | expected_p95_ms | notes
us-west1 | 6 | 2 | 28 | 3 | 300 | 205 | balance between cost and burst handling for west coast peak
us-east1 | 6 | 2 | 30 | 3 | 420 | 208 | longer cooldown handles quick diurnal ramps on east coast
eu-west1 | 4 | 1 | 18 | 2 | 240 | 195 | smaller capacity required most days
ap-southeast1 | 3 | 1 | 14 | 2 | 300 | 250 | bump min for network variance, monitor p95 closely

Cost/efficiency notes (sample math with conservative estimates):
- Instance cost per GPU-hour (on committed Dedicated pools): $2.40 (avg across regions assumed).
- Idle hours/day estimated from traces by policy: if avg_idle_hours_per_day = 1.6 for us-west1 policy E1, incremental cost = 1.6 * n_gpus * $2.40. For a pool of 20 GPUs, incremental daily idle cost ~= $76.8.
- Recommendation: prefer smaller warm_pool (1-2) and tuned step=3 for most regions; increase warm_pool for regions with frequent sub-10-minute bursts tied to product launches.

Failure modes and risk matrix:
- Oscillation (scale-flapping): occurs when cooldowns too short and step sizes large. Mitigation: cooldown >= 240s, cap consecutive scale events to 2 within a 10-minute window, add a short jitter on evaluation intervals.
- Cold-start latency spikes: inadequate warm_pool (0) + model load time. Mitigation: reserve warm_pool for 10% of peak traffic pools; pre-warm critical routes.
- Cost overshoot during sustained growth: max_gpus set too high relative to observed sustained demand. Mitigation: use auto-scaling budgets with alerts and soft caps tied to cost center tags.

Recommended rollout plan (staged):
1) Canary region: apply recommended policy in eu-west1 for 72 hours (low traffic risk), monitor p95, queue depth, and idle-hours.
2) US roll: apply us-west1 policy next with telemetry hooks and a temporary cost guard to roll back if idle-hours exceed 4/day.
3) APAC conservative: apply increased min in ap-southeast1 for only production-critical projects; keep non-critical customers on separate pool.
4) Post-roll evaluation: 2-week review, then commit to policy as baseline and codify in infra-as-code.

Runbook quick checks (for on-call / SRE):
- If p95 > 300ms for > 5 minutes: check warm_pool utilization and recent scale events; increase warm_pool by 1 as temporary mitigation and set incident tag.
- If autoscaler scales > 80% of max for > 10 minutes: open an incident, investigate traffic source, consider temporary burst-capacity increase from dedicated spare pool.
- If oscillation detected: revert cooldown to >= 420s and reduce step size by 1.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: land warm-pool prewarm scripts in infra repo (PR target: infra/pull/332) — due 2026-03-08
- Miguel: add autoscaler jitter and consecutive-scale-cap guardrails (JIRA-INFRA-1289) — due 2026-03-05
- Sofia: dashboard tiles for idle-hours by pool and by tag, alert when idle-hours/day > 3 — due 2026-03-10
- Evan: run 48-hour canary in eu-west1 and publish metrics (CONFLUENCE-ENG/Autoscale-Runbook-4021) — due 2026-03-15

Notes to self (rough):
- Follow up: test with shorter model load path (quantized checkpoint) to reduce cold-start by ~30% (obs from E1).
- Consider integrating a short-lived burst credit system tied to product release windows so we can keep warm pools small most of the time but temporarily expand without changing min/max.
- Capture per-route token/s distribution to inform per-route scheduling into smaller granularity pools.

End of runbook sheet.
